n: The fool says in his heart, “There is no God” — usually meaning not a philosophical atheist but someone who lives as if God doesn’t matter. Psalm 53 is nearly identical.

f.g: Hebrew nabal — morally foolish, someone who rejects God’s ways (compare Nabal in 1 Samuel 25:25).

n: The Lord looks down from heaven to see if anyone understands and seeks him.

f.w: The LORD looked down from heaven

n: All have turned aside and become corrupt; no one does good, not even one. Paul quotes this to show that everyone needs Christ’s grace.

f.w: there is none that doeth good, no, not one

f.g: Corrupt, gone bad like spoiled milk.

n: Don’t evildoers ever learn? They devour God’s people as casually as eating bread and never call on the Lord.

f.w: who eat up my people as they eat bread

n: Then they will be overwhelmed with terror, for God stands with the righteous.

f.w: God is in the generation of the righteous

n: The wicked mock the plans of the poor, but the Lord is their refuge.
Oh, that salvation for Israel would come from Zion! When the Lord restores his people, Jacob will rejoice. Latter-day Saints also connect this hope with the latter-day gathering.

f.w: the salvation of Israel were come out of Zion
bringeth back the captivity of his people
f.g: Restores the fortunes of his people.
